newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber extends losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber extends losses at close.

text.p: Lack of consumer demand and ample stocks continued to drag down Malaysian rubber prices at the close, dealers said.
"The market is still dropping and people are waiting for more attractive lower levels," a dealer said, adding that players stayed away from the market because of more raw materials.
The improved weather conditions had lead to an ample latex stock, dealers said. Buyers are turning their interest to other producing countries, they added.
There was a lack of strong enquiries from European and Asian consumers who were checking current levels, traders said.
Trading houses also lowered their offer prices, quoting the SMR 20 at 293 cents a kg, SMR CV at 356, SMR L at 336, SMR 5 at 304, SMR 10 at 294 and drum latex FOB at 233-234.
At the close, February RSS 1 eased one cent to 298.50 cents ($1.20) a kg and February SMR 20 was down half a cent at 293.50 cents.
